front: Procedure: dwelling general lighting + small appliance + laundry (standard method)
back:
1. Floor area × 3 VA/ft² (Table 220.12)
2. + 1500 VA × 2 small-appliance circuits (220.52(A)) + 1500 VA laundry (220.52(B))
3. Apply Table 220.42: first 3000 VA @ 100 %, 3001–120,000 VA @ 35 %, rest @ 25 %
4. Add range (Table 220.55), dryer (220.54), fixed appliances (220.53, 75 % if ≥ 4), heat or A/C — larger of the two (220.60) @ 100 %

front: Worked: 2400 ft² dwelling — general lighting after demand
back:
2400 × 3 = 7200 VA
+ 3000 (small appliance) + 1500 (laundry) = 11,700 VA
First 3000 @ 100 % = 3000
Remaining 8700 @ 35 % = 3045
Demand load = 6045 VA

front: Worked: one 12 kW range; one 15 kW range; branch-circuit minimum
back:
≤ 12 kW, one range: column C = 8 kW demand
15 kW: 8 kW + 5 % per kW over 12 → 8 × 1.15 = 9.2 kW (Note 1)
Branch: 9200 ÷ 240 = 38.3 A → 40 A circuit; 210.19(A)(3) sets 40 A minimum for 8¾ kW and larger ranges anyway

front: Worked: dryer load and neutral for a 5.5 kW dryer
back:
Dryer: nameplate or 5000 VA, whichever is larger → 5500 VA (220.54)
Table 220.54: 1–4 dryers @ 100 %
Neutral for ranges/dryers: 70 % of the demand → 5500 × 0.70 = 3850 VA (220.61(B)(1))

front: Worked: optional method — 2000 ft² dwelling, 12 kW range, 5 kW dryer, 4.5 kW water heater, 5 kW A/C vs 10 kW electric heat
Worked: 60 general-purpose receptacles in an office — load and demand
back:
180 VA per yoke (220.14(I)) → 60 × 180 = 10,800 VA
Table 220.44 (nondwelling receptacles): first 10 kVA @ 100 %, remainder @ 50 %
10,000 + 400 = 10,400 VA
One quad = 2 yokes = 360 VA; a multi-outlet assembly is per 220.14(H)

front: Procedure: size conductor + OCPD for a continuous load (worked: 20 A continuous + 8 A noncontinuous)
back:
Minimum = 125 % × continuous + 100 % × noncontinuous
= 25 + 8 = 33 A
OCPD: next standard size ≥ 33 A → 35 A (240.6(A))
Conductor: ampacity ≥ 33 A after corrections; 10 AWG Cu 75 °C (35 A) works, but 240.4(D) caps 10 AWG at 30 A → 8 AWG

front: Worked: a conductor's corrected ampacity is 115 A — which OCPD? The rounding rules
back:
No standard size at 115 A → the next size up, 125 A, is permitted (240.4(B)) when: ≤ 800 A, not a multi-outlet branch circuit for cord-and-plug loads, and the conductor isn't already capped by 240.4(D)
Above 800 A: OCPD must be ≤ the conductor ampacity (240.4(C))
Standard sizes to recall (240.6(A)): 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 60 70 80 90 100 110 125 150 175 200 225 250 300 350 400 450 500 600

front: Worked: GEC for a 200 A service with 3/0 Cu service conductors; and if the only electrode is a ground rod
back:
3/0 Cu → Table 250.66 row '2/0 or 3/0' → 4 AWG Cu GEC
Rod/pipe/plate only: GEC never required larger than 6 AWG Cu (250.66(A))
Concrete-encased electrode only: not larger than 4 AWG Cu (250.66(B))
Parallel sets: add the CM of one phase to pick the row

front: Worked: EGC when 100 A feeder conductors are upsized from 3 AWG to 1 AWG Cu for voltage drop
back:
Base EGC for a 100 A OCPD = 8 AWG Cu (Table 250.122)
Upsize in proportion to circular mils (250.122(B)): 1 AWG 83,690 ÷ 3 AWG 52,620 = 1.59
8 AWG 16,510 × 1.59 = 26,258 cmil — just over 6 AWG (26,240) → 4 AWG Cu
EGC never needs to be larger than the circuit conductors (250.122(A))

front: Worked: supply-side bonding jumper for 600 kcmil Cu service conductors; and for 2 × 500 kcmil per phase
back:
600 kcmil Cu → row 'over 350 through 600' → 1/0 Cu
2 × 500 kcmil per phase = 1000 kcmil → row 'over 600 through 1100' → 2/0 Cu
Over 1100 kcmil Cu: jumper ≥ 12½ % of the largest phase conductor area (Table 250.102(C)(1) Note 1)
Parallel sets: add the areas of one phase to pick the row

front: Worked: 200 A dwelling service — minimum conductor using the 83 % rule
back:
200 × 0.83 = 166 A required ampacity (310.12(A), services 100–400 A to a single dwelling)
Table 310.16, 75 °C: 2/0 Cu = 175 A ✔ (vs 3/0 without the rule)
4/0 Al = 180 A ✔
Feeder to the whole dwelling load qualifies too (310.12(B))

10-ft tap: ampacity ≥ calculated load AND ≥ the device it feeds; if leaving the enclosure, ≥ 10 % of the feeder OCPD; ends in a single OCPD or device; in a raceway
25-ft tap: ampacity ≥ ⅓ of feeder OCPD; ends in a single OCPD rated ≤ tap ampacity; protected from damage
Worked: 400 A feeder → 25-ft tap needs ≥ 133 A (1/0 Cu at 150 A)

front: Worked: biggest cord-and-plug load on a 20 A receptacle; receptacle choices on a 30 A circuit
back:
Single cord-and-plug load ≤ 80 % of the receptacle rating: 20 A → 16 A; 15 A → 12 A; 30 A → 24 A
30 A branch circuit (2+ receptacles): 30 A receptacles only
20 A circuit: 15 or 20 A receptacles; 15 A circuit: 15 A only; 40/50 A circuit: 40 or 50 A

front: Worked: feeder neutral for a 500 A unbalanced load (no nonlinear loads)
back:
First 200 A @ 100 % = 200
Remainder 300 A @ 70 % = 210
Neutral demand = 410 A
No reduction for the portion from nonlinear loads or for 3-wire 1φ from a 4-wire 3φ wye (220.61(C))

front: Worked: feeder for 60 A continuous + 40 A noncontinuous
back:
Conductor: 125 % × 60 + 40 = 115 A min (215.2(A)(1))
OCPD: same 115 A min → 125 A standard (215.3, 240.6)
If the OCPD is 100 %-rated and listed: conductors and OCPD at 100 % (exception)
Table 310.16 75 °C: 1 AWG Cu = 130 A ✔

Service conductors sized to the calculated load per Art. 220 (230.42(A)); continuous loads × 125 %
Disconnect rating: one-family dwelling ≥ 100 A (230.79(C)); 2 circuits ≥ 30 A; one circuit ≥ 15 A; everything else ≥ 60 A
Max 6 disconnects — 2020: each in its own enclosure or compartment (230.71)
